q: Which term fits this definition: “Previously developed land that may be contaminated but has potential for redevelopment”?
n: Brownfield Site: Previously developed land that may be contaminated but has potential for redevelopment.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The decline of the social, physical, and economic fabric of a city, usually located in the oldest part of the settlement”?
n: Urban Decay: The decline of the social, physical, and economic fabric of a city, usually located in the oldest part of the settlement.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Planning for the society, present and future, that involves physical characteristics, topography, climate, geographical location, soil condition, existing bodies of water, natural and man-made ecology, economics growth, employment, political and social structure”?
n: Regional Planning: Planning for the society, present and future, that involves physical characteristics, topography, climate, geographical location, soil condition, existing bodies of water, natural and man-made ecology, economics growth, employment, political and social structure.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The process whereby one change sets in motion a sequence of events that result in decline or growth”?
n: Multiplier Effect: The process whereby one change sets in motion a sequence of events that result in decline or growth.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Undeveloped land in a city or rural area used for agriculture or landscape design, now considered for urban development”?
n: Greenfield Site: Undeveloped land in a city or rural area used for agriculture or landscape design, now considered for urban development.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A farm in which a group of farmers pool their land, domestic animals, and agricultural implements, retaining as private property enough only for the members' own requirements”?
n: Collective Farm: A farm in which a group of farmers pool their land, domestic animals, and agricultural implements, retaining as private property enough only for the members' own requirements.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A planning tool used to designate permitted land uses in specific areas, e.g. residential, commercial, industrial”?
n: Zoning: A planning tool used to designate permitted land uses in specific areas, e.g. residential, commercial, industrial.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A group of unplanned shelters constructed from cheap or waste materials (such as cardboard, wood, or cloth), commonly located on the outskirts of cities in poor countries or on derelict land”?
n: Shanty Town: A group of unplanned shelters constructed from cheap or waste materials (such as cardboard, wood, or cloth), commonly located on the outskirts of cities in poor countries or on derelict land.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A type of building development and regulatory process that is a large-scale project not required to follow standard zoning rules”?
n: Planned Unit Development (PUD): A type of building development and regulatory process that is a large-scale project not required to follow standard zoning rules.

q: Which term fits this definition: “An area planned for industry, where space is available for large buildings and further expansion”?
n: Industrial Estate: An area planned for industry, where space is available for large buildings and further expansion.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The dispersion of a population away from a central point”?
n: Decentralization: The dispersion of a population away from a central point.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The practice of farming, including the cultivation of the soil for raising crops and the raising of domesticated animals”?
n: Agriculture: The practice of farming, including the cultivation of the soil for raising crops and the raising of domesticated animals.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The technical and political process of managing the physical growth and land-use of a self-contained settlement, defined by statutory zoning”?
o: Town Planning (Urban Design or Settlement Planning)
n: Town Planning (Urban Design or Settlement Planning): The technical and political process of managing the physical growth and land-use of a self-contained settlement, defined by statutory zoning.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A chain of conditions in which deprivation, once started, keeps reproducing itself unless there is outside intervention; often found in inner-city areas and shanty towns”?
n: Poverty Cycle (Development Trap): A set of factors or events by which poverty, once started, is likely to continue unless there is outside intervention; often found in inner-city areas and shanty towns.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The process of managing land resources to meet urban, economic, and environmental goals”?
n: Land Use Planning: The process of managing land resources to meet urban, economic, and environmental goals.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The paid jobs that people do”?
n: Employment: The paid jobs that people do.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A low-density office development often established by private companies on greenfield sites, tending to be located near motorway junctions with a high proportion of high-tech firms”?
n: Business Park: A low-density office development often established by private companies on greenfield sites, tending to be located near motorway junctions with a high proportion of high-tech firms.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Simplified diagrams used by planners to explain how cities grow and how different land uses (like housing, factories, and shops) are arranged”?
n: Urban Model: Simplified diagrams used by planners to explain how cities grow and how different land uses (like housing, factories, and shops) are arranged.

q: Which term fits this definition: “An urban settlement whose main function is to cater for tourism of one type or another”?
n: Resort Town: An urban settlement whose main function is to cater for tourism of one type or another.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Urban development that blends residential, commercial, cultural, and industrial uses”?
n: Mixed-Use Development: Urban development that blends residential, commercial, cultural, and industrial uses.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A point within an area where economic activity is concentrated; this may encourage further development in the surrounding area through the multiplier effect, especially in areas of industrial decline”?
n: Growth Pole: A point within an area where economic growth is concentrated; this growth may encourage further development in the surrounding area through the multiplier effect, especially in areas of industrial decline.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A grassroots-oriented process focused on the social, economic, and physical well-being of a specific neighborhood, defined by its high level of public participation”?
n: Community Planning: A grassroots-oriented process focused on the social, economic, and physical well-being of a specific neighborhood or community of interest, defined by its high level of public participation.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A natural airflow strategy where warm air rises and escapes through the roof ridge, pulling cooler air in through lower openings like the ventanillas”?
n: Stack Effect Ventilation: A natural ventilation strategy where warm air rises and escapes through the roof ridge, pulling cooler air in through lower openings like the ventanillas.

q: Which term fits this definition: “An area of poor-quality housing, typically found in parts of the inner city in rich countries and older parts of cities in poor countries; densely populated with inadequate services”?
n: Slum: An area of poor-quality housing, typically found in parts of the inner city in rich countries and older parts of cities in poor countries; densely populated with inadequate services.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The number of people inhabiting a country, region, area, or town; population statistics are derived from registration of birth and death and from censuses”?
n: Population: The number of people inhabiting a country, region, area, or town; population statistics are derived from registration of birth and death and from censuses.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The place where industry is found; industries have traditionally located near their markets, raw materials, or sources of labour, generally choosing where they can make the most profit”?
n: Industrial Location: The place where industry is found; industries have traditionally located near their markets, raw materials, or sources of labour, generally choosing where they can make the most profit.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The study of population”?
n: Demography: The study of population.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Money or resources given or lent on favourable terms to developing countries; short-term aid relieves emergencies like famine, while long-term aid promotes economic development”?
n: Aid: Money or resources given or lent on favourable terms to developing countries; short-term aid relieves emergencies like famine, while long-term aid promotes economic development.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Human settlements with high population density and a built environment consisting of infrastructure, residential, and commercial buildings”?
n: Urban: Human settlements with high population density and a built environment consisting of infrastructure, residential, and commercial buildings.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A city that is far the largest within a country or area, holding a larger proportion of population, economic activity, and social functions than other settlements in the area”?
n: Primate City: A city that is far the largest within a country or area, holding a larger proportion of population, economic activity, and social functions than other settlements in the area.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Also called Ribbon Development; housing that has grown up along a route such as a road”?
n: Linear Development: Also called Ribbon Development; housing that has grown up along a route such as a road.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The conditions affecting a particular organism, including physical surroundings, climate, and influences of other living organisms”?
n: Environment: The conditions affecting a particular organism, including physical surroundings, climate, and influences of other living organisms.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The area of a town or city where most commercial activity is found, dominated by shops, offices, entertainment venues, and government buildings; characterized by high rent and rates, tall buildings, and chain stores”?
n: Central Business District (CBD): The area of a town or city where most commercial activity is found, dominated by shops, offices, entertainment venues, and government buildings; characterized by high rent and rates, tall buildings, and chain stores.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A comprehensive, large-scale system design for high-density environments, defined by the integration of complex infrastructure networks (transportation, water, power, and housing) within a city boundary”?
n: Urban Planning: A comprehensive, large-scale system design for high-density environments, defined by the integration of complex infrastructure networks (transportation, water, power, and housing) within a city boundary.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Geographic areas located outside towns and cities, characterized by low population density and large open spaces, with primary economic activity typically centered on agriculture, forestry, or mining”?
n: Rural: Geographic areas located outside towns and cities, characterized by low population density and large open spaces, with primary economic activity typically centered on agriculture, forestry, or mining.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Too many people for the resources available in an area (such as food, land, and water)”?
n: Overpopulation: Too many people for the resources available in an area (such as food, land, and water).

q: Which term fits this definition: “Manufacturing that processes large amounts of bulky raw materials, e.g. iron and steel making, shipbuilding, etc”?
n: Heavy Industry: Industry that processes large amounts of bulky raw materials, e.g. iron and steel industry, shipbuilding, etc.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Action taken to protect and preserve the natural world, usually from pollution, over-exploration, and other harmful features of human activity”?
n: Conservation: Action taken to protect and preserve the natural world, usually from pollution, over-exploration, and other harmful features of human activity.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A passive design strategy using deep roof overhangs and window awnings so the building self-shades, preventing the building envelope from absorbing solar heat.”?
n: Shading and Media Aguas: A passive design strategy using deep roof overhangs and window awnings so the building self-shades, preventing the building envelope from absorbing solar heat.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The area surrounding a settlement that is affected by the settlement's activities, which may be mapped using catchment areas, local-newspaper circulation, delivery areas, and public transport destinations”?
n: Sphere of Influence: The area surrounding a settlement that is affected by the settlement's activities, which may be mapped using catchment areas, local-newspaper circulation, delivery areas, and public transport destinations.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Measures taken by some governments to limit the growth of their countries' population by trying to reduce the birth rate”?
n: Population Control: Measures taken by some governments to limit the growth of their countries' population by trying to reduce the birth rate.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Facilities that service an industrial economy, e.g. roads, railways, telephones, energy and water supply”?
n: Infrastructure: Facilities that service an industrial economy, e.g. roads, railways, telephones, energy and water supply.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A region with substandard economic performance, perhaps due to a change in industrial structure, such as a decline in manufacturing industry”?
n: Depressed Area: A region with substandard economic performance, perhaps due to a change in industrial structure, such as a decline in manufacturing industry.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The assumption that land value and rent decrease as distance from the central business district increases”?
n: Bid-Rent Theory: The assumption that land value and rent decrease as distance from the central business district increases.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The process whereby an increasing proportion of a region's population becomes concentrated in urban areas”?
n: Urbanization: The process whereby an increasing proportion of a region's population becomes concentrated in urban areas.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Government-funded homes provided to low-income families”?
n: Public Housing: Government-funded housing provided to low-income families.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A settlement with a permanent or periodic trading place that acts as a selling point for goods produced in the surrounding hinterlands”?
n: Market Town: A settlement with a permanent or periodic market that acts as a selling point for goods produced in the surrounding hinterlands.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A port, or sometimes a zone within a port, where cargo may be accepted for handling, processing, and reshipment without the imposition of tariffs and taxes”?
n: Free Port: A port, or sometimes a zone within a port, where cargo may be accepted for handling, processing, and reshipment without the imposition of tariffs and taxes.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A settlement, or service centre, to which people travel from the surrounding area (hinterland) to obtain various goods or services”?
n: Central Place: A place, or service centre, to which people travel from the surrounding area (hinterland) to obtain various goods or services.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The adaptation of existing buildings in towns and cities to meet changes in economic, social, and environmental requirements rather than demolishing them; gentrification is one option for raising an area's social and economic status”?
n: Urban Renewal: The adaptation of existing buildings in towns and cities to meet changes in economic, social, and environmental requirements rather than demolishing them; gentrification is one option for raising an area's social and economic status.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The loss of people from remote country areas to cities; it is an effect of migration”?
n: Rural Depopulation: The loss of people from remote country areas to cities; it is an effect of migration.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The process of removing vehicle traffic from a street or district and converting it for the exclusive use of people on foot or bicycles, to improve air quality, safety, and walkability”?
n: Pedestrianization: The process of removing vehicle traffic from a street or district and converting it for the exclusive use of people on foot or bicycles, to improve air quality, safety, and walkability.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Areas that are served by a port or settlement (the central place) and are included in its sphere of influence”?
n: Hinterland: Areas that are served by a port or settlement (the central place) and are included in its sphere of influence.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Areas with different degrees of economic development; some regions hold concentrated capital, infrastructure, and development, while outlying regions lack these resources”?
o: Town Planning (Urban Design or Settlement Planning)
n: Core and Periphery: Areas with different degrees of economic development; core areas are where capital, infrastructure, and development are concentrated, while periphery areas lack these resources.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The ease with which a place may be reached; such an area generally has a well-developed transport network and is centrally located or at a route centre”?
n: Accessibility: The ease with which a place may be reached; an area with high accessibility generally has a well-developed transport network and is centrally located or at a route centre.

q: Which term fits this definition: “An illegal occupant of a building or land”?
n: Squatter: An illegal occupant of a building or land.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The number of people living in each area, usually expressed as people per square kilometer, providing a useful means for comparing population distribution”?
n: Population Density: The number of people living in each area, usually expressed as people per square kilometer, providing a useful means for comparing population distribution.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The type of technology that utilizes inanimate sources of energy for driving its tools and sources of energy to produce goods and services”?
n: Industrialism: The type of technology that utilizes inanimate sources of energy for driving its tools and sources of energy to produce goods and services.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A settlement made up of buildings scattered over a wide area”?
n: Dispersed Settlement: A settlement made up of buildings scattered over a wide area.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The number of live babies born per 1000 of the population of an area over the period of a year”?
n: Birth Rate: The number of live births per 1000 of the population of an area over the period of a year.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The physical 'symptom' of a declining city, referring to the visible deterioration of buildings and public spaces, characterized by abandoned structures, trash-accumulating lots, and disrepaired infrastructure, often lowering nearby property values”?
n: Urban Blight: The physical 'symptom' of a declining city, referring to the visible deterioration of buildings and public spaces, characterized by abandoned structures, trash-accumulating lots, and disrepaired infrastructure, often lowering nearby property values.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Anything that tends to attract people to an area, such as higher wages, better housing, and better education opportunities”?
n: Pull Factor: Any factor that tends to attract people to an area, such as higher wages, better housing, and better education opportunities.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Massive urban metropolitan areas with a total population of more than 10 million people, often serving as primary economic and political hubs but facing challenges with housing, traffic, and waste management”?
n: Megacities: Massive urban metropolitan areas with a total population of more than 10 million people, often serving as primary economic and political hubs but facing challenges with housing, traffic, and waste management.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The process of transforming a lower-income neighborhood through investment and new residents, often displacing the original community”?
n: Gentrification: The process of transforming a lower-income neighborhood through investment and new residents, often displacing the original community.

q: Which term fits this definition: “An important, or high-order, urban settlement”?
n: City: An important, or high-order, urban settlement.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The outward spread of built-up areas caused by their expansion”?
n: Urban Sprawl: The outward spread of built-up areas caused by their expansion.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A place where people live, varying in size from isolated dwellings to the largest cities”?
n: Settlement: A place where people live, varying in size from isolated dwellings to the largest cities.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A country-dweller engaged in small-scale farming, normally owning or renting a small amount of land, aiming to be self-sufficient and sell surplus supplies locally”?
n: Peasant: A country-dweller engaged in small-scale farming, normally owning or renting a small amount of land, aiming to be self-sufficient and sell surplus supplies locally.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A concept representing the architectural and philosophical quest to create a utopian environment that balances order, social harmony, and functionality”?
n: Ideal Cities: A concept representing the architectural and philosophical quest to create a utopian environment that balances order, social harmony, and functionality.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The movement of people and employment away from urban areas to smaller towns and villages in a rural location, pushed by factors such as congestion, high land prices, and population pressure”?
n: Counter Urbanization: The movement of people and employment away from urban areas to smaller towns and villages in a rural location, pushed by factors such as congestion, high land prices, and population pressure.

q: Which term fits this definition: “Commercial farming on an industrial scale, often financed by companies whose main interest lies outside agriculture (e.g. multi-national corporations); mechanized, large, highly structured, and reliant on chemicals”?
n: Agribusiness: Commercial farming on an industrial scale, often financed by companies whose main interest lies outside agriculture (e.g. multi-national corporations); mechanized, large, highly structured, and reliant on chemicals.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The tools and know-how, connected with the use of both tools and sources of energy, to produce goods and services”?
n: Technology: The tools and know-how, connected with the use of both tools and sources of energy, to produce goods and services.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The location of people within an area”?
n: Population Distribution: The location of people within an area.

q: Which term fits this definition: “The area that immediately borders the central business district of a town or city; often one of the older parts, which may suffer from decay and neglect leading to social problems”?
n: Inner City: The area that immediately borders the central business district of a town or city; often one of the older parts, which may suffer from decay and neglect leading to social problems.

q: Which term fits this definition: “A link on a topographical map; nodes, or junctions, are formed where edges meet and intersect”?
o: Town Planning (Urban Design or Settlement Planning)
n: Edge: A link on a topographical map; nodes, or junctions, are formed where edges meet and intersect.
